# Minnesota Senate race takes bizarre turn after dark family history uncovered

[Peggy Flanagan's grandfather escaped psychiatric custody twice: report | Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/minnesota-senate-race-takes-bizarre-turn-dark-family-history-uncovered) · 2026-10-18

A dark chapter in the family history of Minnesota Democratic Senate candidate Peggy Flanagan has made its way into the race, but it is unclear whether voters will hold the alleged sins of her long-dead grandfather against her.

Earlier this week, Alpha News revealed the troubled mental health history of Flanagan's grandfather, John Jacob Hartmann, supported by old newspaper accounts and court records. He spent decades in psychiatric custody, escaped twice and was suspected in multiple killings, though never charged.

The reporting comes just weeks before the midterm elections, in which Flanagan, the state's lieutenant governor, faces former television sports reporter Michelle Tafoya in a race to fill the seat of Democrat Tina Smith, who is retiring.

Neither Flanagan nor Tafoya has commented publicly on the matter since the decades-old allegations resurfaced. But the bizarre development has generated a buzz on social media.

Turning Point USA spokesman Andrew Kolvet highlighted the "violent mental illness in Minnesota Democrat Peggy Flanagan's family," in an [X](https://x.com/AndrewKolvet/status/2110383189671956586) post, followed by a photo of Flanagan wearing a shirt that says "Protect trans kids." and Dustin Grage, a columnist with Town Hall, [wrote](https://x.com/GrageDustin/status/2110160636772766027) the report "adds up."

Flanagan has frequently spoken about her upbringing, including being raised by a single mother who relied on SNAP benefits and housing assistance, and the influence of her indigenous father, a tribal land rights activist who helped inspire her own advocacy for Native American communities.

But a lesser-known part of her family history involves Hartmann, who made headlines in [Minneapolis](https://www.foxnews.com/category/us/minneapolis-st-paul) newspapers throughout the 1970s and early 1980s for his time in psychiatric hospitals, his escapes and allegations linking him to at least four killings, which was dredged up by Minnesota-based outlet [Alpha News.](https://alphanews.org/exclusive-peggy-flanagans-grandfather-was-suspected-in-serial-killings-spent-decades-in-mental-hospitals-records-reveal/)

Peggy Flanagan, Minnesota’s lieutenant governor and Senate hopeful, is facing backlash over her progressive activism and outreach amid the state’s sprawling fraud controversy. (Photo by MANDEL NGAN/AFP via Getty Images)

Flanagan was three years old when Hartmann died on Feb. 6, 1983. A Minnesota Star Tribune death notice listed Flanagan’s mother, Patricia Hartmann, and her three sisters — Kathleen, Mary and Margaret — as his surviving daughters. An [obituary](https://www.washburn-mcreavy.com/obituaries/patricia-flanagan-3/#!/Obituary) for Patricia, who died in 2022, listed her maiden name as Hartmann and identified her father as John.

In an [interview](https://www.womenspress.com/peggy-flanagan/) with Minnesota Women’s Press, Flanagan said both her mother and grandmother were single mothers. She described her grandmother as having raised four daughters "at a time when that didn’t happen a lot." Flanagan's mother eventually married Thomas Flanagan, who is identified as [Peggy Flanagan's stepfather](https://www.foxnews.com/category/entertainment/genres/family) in his [obituary](https://obituaries.startribune.com/obituary/thomas-flanagan-1090171612/).

In a Feb. 9, 1983 [article](https://www.newspapers.com/image/190424184/?match=3&terms=%22John%20Hartmann%2C%20suspected%20in%204%20slayings%20but%20never%20tried%2C%20is%20dead%22&search-id=1b81db2b-8d17-4a1f-8355-ec33caff35fd&search-rank=1) announcing Hartmann's death, the newspaper now known as The Minnesota Star Tribune stated that he was committed on Nov. 1, 1951 after his wife filed a petition claiming that he was "mentally ill and dangerous." His commitment came after the body of a man named Theodore Foth was found burning in his room, although Hartmann was never charged in Foth's death. The paper also named Hartmann as a suspect in a 1964 murder of a fellow patient at the Minnesota Security Hospital, but he was never charged.

[death notice of John Hartmann](https://a57.foxnews.com/static.foxnews.com/foxnews.com/content/uploads/2026/10/1200/675/John-Hartmann-death-notice_002.png?ve=1&tl=1)

A Feb. 9 1983 Minnesota Star Tribune Article announcing the death of John Hartmann, maternal grandfather of Peggy Flanagan (Newspapers.com)

Hartmann was transferred to Anoka State Hospital in 1970, but escaped to New Mexico, where the newspaper reported he was suspected in the deaths of a man and woman. However, a 1973 Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals [ruling](https://law.justia.com/cases/federal/appellate-courts/F2/488/1215/422373/) does not mention the alleged murder allegations against Hartmann. Instead, the ruling stated New Mexico authorities picked up Hartmann from a warrant issued by Minnesota Probate Judge Melvin Peterson in September 1970. The authorities found that he was living in the state "without incident and without hiding his identity following his escape in Minnesota." A special prosecutor later released Hartmann, finding that he was "sane and safe to be at large."

Hartmann was apprehended in Colorado for a misdemeanor charge the next year and brought back to Minnesota.

In April 1979, Hartmann failed to return from a visit pass at the Minnesota Security Hospital and fled to Missouri, where he allegedly threatened U.S. District Judge Miles Welton Lord during a phone call. Lord presided over Hartmann’s earlier federal challenge to his involuntary return from Colorado to Minnesota and initially dismissed claims against several Minnesota officials. Hartmann was charged by federal authorities for the alleged threat, according to a 1979 Star Tribune [article.](https://www.newspapers.com/image/187124499/?match=2&terms=Doug%20Stone%2C%20%22Hospital%20Escapee%20Charged%20with%20Crime%22&search-id=1f7aba11-1d8e-45c2-829c-64a0a577d362&search-rank=1)
